lessons.title: Running Social Media Ads for Resellers
lessons.body: Running ads on social media can bring you sales quickly, but you must start small and measure everything. In Africa, the cheapest and most effective platforms for resellers are Facebook and Instagram (using Meta Ads Manager) and TikTok. Start with a budget of $5 per day (about 3,500 Naira or 60 Ghana Cedis). Choose 'Traffic' or 'Engagement' objective first to get people to see your post. Use a clear photo of your product, a short video (15 seconds) showing the product in use, and a caption that includes price, delivery options, and a call to action like 'Send a DM to order'. Target your audience by location (your city), age (18-45), and interests (online shopping, fashion, etc.). Run the ad for 3 days, then check results: if you spent $15 and got 10 messages but no sales, change the photo or caption. If you got 3 sales, increase budget to $10 per day. Use WhatsApp link in your ad so people can message you directly. Always reply fastâwithin 5 minutesâbecause ad leads go cold quickly. Track your spending and sales in a notebook or Excel sheet. Don't run ads without a clear goal. Many resellers fail because they run ads without testing. Test with $5, find what works, then scale. Also, use retargeting later (see Lesson 5). Remember: Facebook ads work best when you have a good product page and real testimonials. Ask happy customers to comment on your ad. That social proof increases sales.

lessons.title: Collaborating with Influencers
lessons.body: Influencer marketing is when you pay or give free products to someone with a following to promote your reselling business. In Africa, you don't need millions of followers. Micro-influencers (1,000 to 10,000 followers) often give better results because their audience trusts them. Find influencers in your niche: fashion, beauty, gadgets, or home goods. Search on Instagram or TikTok using hashtags like #NigerianFashionBlogger, #KenyanYouTuber, or #GhanaianBeauty. Look for engagement (likes and comments) not just follower count. A good engagement rate is 3-5%. Contact them via DM or email. Offer a free product (cost: $10-20) plus a small fee ($10-50) for a post or video. For example, if you sell hair extensions, send a free pack to a hairstylist with 5,000 followers who does tutorials. Ask them to show the installation and mention your WhatsApp number. Track results using a unique promo code or a special link (use Bitly or Linktree). If you get 10 sales from that influencer, you made profit. Build long-term relationships: offer commission (10-20% of sales) instead of flat fee. That way, they are motivated to sell more. Always have a written agreement (even WhatsApp messages) stating what they will post, when, and how you will pay. Avoid influencers who buy fake followersâcheck their comments for real conversations. Also, consider barter: give free products for posts if you have low budget. Many micro-influencers accept that. After the campaign, ask for a testimonial and permission to repost their content. That builds trust for your brand.

lessons.title: Hosting Giveaways and Contests
lessons.body: Giveaways and contests are powerful for growing your social media following and getting new customers. The goal is to get people to engage with your page and share it with friends. A simple giveaway: you give one free product (value $10-30) to one winner. To enter, people must follow your page, like the post, and tag two friends in the comments. That's it. This costs you only the product and shipping. In Africa, giveaways spread fast on WhatsApp and Facebook groups. Announce the giveaway for 5-7 days. Use a clear graphic with the prize photo, rules, and end date. Example: 'Win a free ankara bag! To enter: 1. Follow @yourpage, 2. Like this post, 3. Tag 2 friends. Winner announced Friday 5pm.' After the giveaway, pick a winner using a random comment picker tool (like Comment Picker for Facebook or Instagram). Announce the winner publicly and show you delivering the prize. That builds trust. For contests, ask people to submit a photo or video using your product (e.g., 'Best style with our sneakers'). The prize can be a shopping voucher or free product. Contests get more user-generated content, which you can repost. Important: follow platform rules. Facebook and Instagram allow giveaways but not 'like to win' schemes that require sharing to a personal timeline. Also, avoid making people pay to enterâthat's illegal in many countries. After the giveaway, many new followers will unfollow. That's normal. But some will stay and become customers. To keep them, send a welcome message with a discount code. Run giveaways every 2-3 months. Budget $20-50 per giveaway. Track how many new followers and sales you get. If you get 100 new followers and 5 sales, it's worth it.

lessons.title: Building an Email List from Social Media
lessons.body: Email marketing is not deadâespecially in Africa where people check email on their phones daily. But building an email list from social media requires a clear incentive. You can't just say 'subscribe to my newsletter.' You must offer something valuable: a discount code (10% off first order), a free guide ('How to choose the right wig'), or early access to sales. Use a free email tool like Mailchimp (free up to 500 subscribers) or Brevo (formerly Sendinblue). Create a simple sign-up form and link it in your Instagram bio, Facebook page, and TikTok bio. Also, post a call-to-action in your stories: 'Swipe up to get 10% off' (if you have the swipe-up feature) or 'Click the link in bio.' Another method: run a giveaway where entry requires email sign-up. For example: 'Win a free phone case! Enter by dropping your email in the comments.' But be carefulâpublic emails can be scraped. Better to use a landing page (like Linktree or Carrd) where they enter email. When someone buys from you, ask for their email at checkout. If you sell via WhatsApp, after delivery, send a message: 'Thanks for your order! Join our VIP list for exclusive discounts: [link]'. Send emails once a week or every two weeks. Content ideas: new arrivals, customer testimonials, flash sales, and tips related to your products. Personalize with their name. Keep emails short and mobile-friendly. Use a clear subject line like '50% off today only' or 'New arrivals for you'. Track open rates (aim for 20-30%) and click rates (2-5%). If low, test different subject lines. Email is your own platformâyou don't lose it if social media changes. Start building today.

lessons.title: Retargeting Past Customers
lessons.body: Retargeting (or remarketing) means showing ads to people who already interacted with your businessâvisited your page, messaged you, or bought before. It's cheaper than finding new customers because they already know you. On Facebook and Instagram, you can create a Custom Audience from people who engaged with your page or website in the last 30, 90, or 180 days. For example, if someone messaged you on WhatsApp but didn't buy, you can show them an ad with a discount code. To do this: go to Meta Ads Manager, create a new audience, choose 'Engagement' and select 'Facebook Page' or 'Instagram Business Profile'. Then run an ad with a special offer: 'Still thinking? Get 10% off your first order. Use code THANKYOU10.' You can also retarget past customers with a new product. If someone bought a phone case, show them a screen protector. Use WhatsApp Business to send broadcast messages to past customers (but only if they opted in). Send a message like: 'Hi [Name], we have new arrivals. As a past customer, you get free delivery this week.' Keep it personal. Another tactic: create a lookalike audience from your past customers. Facebook will find new people similar to them. That's powerful for scaling. For retargeting to work, you need a pixel on your website (if you have one) or use engagement audiences. If you only sell via WhatsApp, you can manually save customer numbers and send them offers via broadcast lists. Always track results: if you spend $10 on retargeting and get 3 sales, that's a 300% return. Retargeting works best with a clear deadline: 'Offer ends Sunday.' Don't over-messageâonce a week is enough. Respect privacy: never share customer data. Use retargeting to build loyalty, not to annoy.

lessons.title: Scaling from Solo to Team
lessons.body: When your reselling business grows, you can't do everything alone. You need to scale from solo to team. Start by identifying tasks you can delegate: packing orders, replying to DMs, posting content, and handling deliveries. Your first hire should be a virtual assistant (VA) or a part-time packer. In Africa, you can find VAs on Facebook groups (e.g., 'Virtual Assistants Nigeria') or platforms like Upwork. Pay $50-100 per month for 20 hours a week. Train them with clear checklists: how to respond to common questions, how to package products, and how to update your inventory sheet. Use free tools like Google Sheets for inventory, Trello for tasks, and WhatsApp for communication. Next, hire a content creator or social media manager. They can schedule posts using Meta Business Suite (free) and engage with followers. Pay them based on results: e.g., $50 per month plus 5% of sales from their posts. For deliveries, partner with a local courier (like GIG Logistics in Nigeria, or Bolt Delivery in Kenya). That frees your time. As you grow, consider hiring a customer service rep and a marketer. But don't hire too fast. Only hire when your profit can cover the salary for at least 3 months. Also, document everything: write down your processes in a Google Doc. That makes training easy. Set up a simple accounting system: track income and expenses in a spreadsheet. Pay yourself a salary. Reinvest 30% of profit into ads and inventory. Build a team culture of honesty and speed. Meet weekly (online) to review numbers. With a team, you can handle more orders, run more ads, and expand to new cities. Start small: hire one person for your biggest pain point. Then grow step by step.

quiz.q: What is the recommended starting daily budget for a reseller's first social media ad?
quiz.explanation: Starting with $5 per day allows you to test without risking too much money.

quiz.q: Which objective should a reseller choose first when running a Facebook ad?
quiz.explanation: Traffic or Engagement objectives are cheaper and help you get initial visibility and messages.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of micro-influencers for resellers?
options: A) They have millions of followers
D) They work for large brands only
quiz.explanation: Micro-influencers have smaller but more engaged audiences, leading to better trust and results.

quiz.q: How can you track sales from an influencer collaboration?
options: B) Use a unique promo code or link
quiz.explanation: A unique promo code or link (e.g., via Bitly) lets you directly measure how many sales came from that influencer.

quiz.q: What is a common rule for a social media giveaway?
options: A) Require people to pay to enter
B) Ask people to tag friends
C) Force them to share on their personal timeline
D) Make it last for 30 days
quiz.explanation: Tagging friends is a standard and allowed entry method that helps spread the word.

quiz.q: Why is it important to announce the winner of a giveaway publicly?
options: B) To build trust and show legitimacy
D) To avoid shipping the prize
quiz.explanation: Publicly announcing and showing delivery proves you are honest and real, which builds trust.

quiz.q: Which tool is recommended for picking a random giveaway winner?
quiz.explanation: Comment Picker is a free tool that randomly selects a winner from comments on Facebook or Instagram.

quiz.q: What should you offer to encourage people to join your email list?
options: B) A discount code or free guide
C) A free product for everyone
quiz.explanation: An incentive like a discount or free guide gives people a reason to share their email.

quiz.q: Which free email marketing tool is suggested for beginners?
quiz.explanation: Mailchimp is free for up to 500 subscribers and easy to use for beginners.

quiz.q: What is a good open rate for email marketing?
quiz.explanation: An open rate of 20-30% is considered good for small businesses.

quiz.q: What is retargeting?
options: A) Showing ads to new people
B) Showing ads to people who already interacted with your business
quiz.explanation: Retargeting focuses on people who have already engaged with your page, website, or messages.

quiz.q: How can you create a retargeting audience on Facebook?
options: A) Use Custom Audience from engagement
quiz.explanation: Facebook allows you to create a Custom Audience based on people who engaged with your page or posts.

quiz.q: What is a good frequency for retargeting messages?
quiz.explanation: Once a week is enough to remind customers without annoying them.

quiz.q: What is a lookalike audience?
options: A) People who look like you
B) New people similar to your past customers
quiz.explanation: Facebook uses your existing audience to find new people with similar characteristics.

quiz.q: What is the first step to scale from solo to team?
quiz.explanation: You must first figure out which tasks are taking your time and can be done by someone else.

quiz.q: Where can you find virtual assistants in Africa?
options: A) Facebook groups like 'Virtual Assistants Nigeria'
quiz.explanation: Facebook groups are common places to find and hire VAs in many African countries.

quiz.q: What is a recommended payment structure for a social media manager?
options: B) Base pay plus commission on sales
quiz.explanation: A base pay plus commission motivates them to generate sales and ensures they have stable income.

quiz.q: Which tool is suggested for inventory management?
quiz.explanation: Google Sheets is free, easy to use, and accessible for tracking inventory.

quiz.q: What should you do before hiring someone?
options: A) Ensure profit covers salary for 3 months
quiz.explanation: You need to be sure your business can afford the new salary for at least 3 months to avoid financial strain.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of documenting processes?
quiz.explanation: Written processes help new team members learn quickly and ensure consistency.

quiz.q: What percentage of profit is suggested for reinvestment?
quiz.explanation: Reinvesting 30% of profit into ads and inventory helps the business grow sustainably.

quiz.q: Which platform is best for retargeting past customers via direct message?
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp Business allows you to send broadcast messages to customers who opted in.

quiz.q: What is a key rule for influencer agreements?
quiz.explanation: A written agreement clarifies deliverables, timelines, and payment, preventing misunderstandings.

quiz.q: What should you check to ensure an influencer has real followers?
quiz.explanation: Real engagement shows in comments; fake followers often have generic or no comments.

quiz.q: What is a good engagement rate for a micro-influencer?
quiz.explanation: 3-5% engagement rate is considered good for micro-influencers.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake in giveaways?
options: A) Making people pay to enter
quiz.explanation: Charging entry fees is illegal in many places and against platform rules.

quiz.q: What is a good way to keep new followers after a giveaway?
options: B) Send a welcome message with a discount
quiz.explanation: A welcome message with a discount encourages new followers to become customers.

quiz.q: What is the recommended frequency for running giveaways?
quiz.explanation: Running giveaways every 2-3 months keeps excitement without overwhelming your audience or budget.

quiz.q: What is a key metric to track for email marketing?
quiz.explanation: Open rate tells you how many people actually opened your email, indicating subject line effectiveness.

quiz.q: What should you do if your email open rate is low?
quiz.explanation: Testing subject lines helps you learn what resonates with your audience and improve open rates.
